A backup is a second copy of a value that is already in storage, so it is the write most likely to hit the quota. Each backup also overwrites the previous one. Storage holds a corrupt or partly unreadable 3 MB 'notes' value in a ~5 MB quota. On load, setItem(BACKUP_KEY) throws QuotaExceededError and is swallowed. store.js:50 loadNotes never checks data.version, so data written by a newer schema is read as version 1 and then overwritten in the old shape. A newer build saves {version: 2, notes: [...]} with extra fields or a different note shape. This build loads it, normalizeNote drops the unknown fields, and the next edit saves it back as version 1. The newer data is lost and no backup is made, because the backup only happens on parse failure or skipped notes.

Code review

Branch main...HEAD, commit b1cc2d5, four new files. There is no CLAUDE.md in the repo, so I checked for bugs only. The change is small, so I read the diff myself and did not launch the subagent pipeline.

1. Stored XSS: note titles are written into innerHTML unescaped (app.js:10, also app.js:46)

app.js:126 flushSave sets updated = Date.now() and re-sorts the list even when the title and body are unchanged. It also calls selectNote and deleteNote without checking that anything changed. The user types a character and deletes it again within 500 ms. The note is marked as newly updated and jumps to the top of the list with no real change. The 'Saved' status then misleads about activity.

app.js:84 Every list render destroys the focused button, so keyboard and screen-reader focus is lost on opening or deleting a note. renderList rebuilds every <li> and button on each call. selectNote (app.js:100) and deleteNote (app.js:121) call it after a button was activated. Nothing restores focus or moves it to the editor (only createNote focuses, at app.js:109). The editor section comes after the whole nav in DOM order (index.html:12-26). WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order (Level A). Keyboard only: Tab to the 40th note's 'open' button and press Enter. The button is removed from the DOM, focus falls to <body>, and the next Tab starts at the top of the page. To reach the title field the user tabs through the search box, New note and up to 80 list buttons. After pressing Delete, focus is likewise lost. A screen-reader user is dropped back to the top of the document.

store.js:30 Backup of corrupt data can fail silently while the user is told it was kept. backupRaw (store.js:29-31) swallows the setItem error and returns nothing. Its callers at store.js:47-48, 52-53 and 65-67 then return a problem string saying the data 'was kept under "notes-backup"'. The comment claims the load message reports the failure; it does not, because the message is written as if the backup succeeded. The raw value is already held under notes, so writing the backup needs about the same space again, and it fails once the stored data is more than about half of the quota. The first edit then overwrites STORAGE_KEY (store.js:75). Stored data is over 50% of the quota and fails JSON.parse, or holds one non-object entry. backupRaw throws QuotaExceededError and is swallowed. The page says the data was kept under 'notes-backup'. The user creates a note, saveNotes replaces the key, and the original data is gone with no copy.

app.js:12 Delete is a clickable div, hidden until mouse hover: not reachable by keyboard, touch or screen reader (WCAG 2.1.1, 4.1.2). Traced. The control is a div with no tabindex, role or accessible name, and its glyph is the only content. styles.css:12 sets .del { opacity: 0; } shown only on li:hover. The list items themselves are li elements with a click handler, also not focusable, so notes cannot be opened by keyboard either. Keyboard-only user: Tab goes search, New note, title, body and never reaches a note or its delete control, so no existing note can be opened or deleted. Touch user: there is no hover, so the invisible delete is a hidden tap target. Screen reader: the control is not announced.

Validation (steps 5 and 6): with nothing flagged, there was nothing to validate or filter.

The agents did mention three behaviours that are not definite bugs, so I left them out:

app.js:187 createNote leaves an active search filter in place, so the new note is selected in the editor but missing from the list. The user types 'foo' in search, then clicks New note. The 'Untitled' note is created and selected but renderList filters it out. The sidebar shows 'No notes match' or no current item, with an editor open on an invisible note. If they retitle it to something that doesn't match 'foo', it disappears from view and they can't find it.

Pending-save handling: a save captures its note id and values when the user types. Switching notes, creating one, deleting one, or hiding the page flushes it first, so a delayed save can't land on the wrong note.

store.js:75 Every save overwrites the whole notes array from one tab's stale memory, so a second tab silently deletes the first tab's notes. saveNotes writes the entire in-memory array under one key. app.js loads once (app.js:17-18) and never listens for the 'storage' event or re-reads before writing (app.js:33). Driven with Playwright in one browser context: tab A created Alpha; tab B loaded and saw ['Alpha']; tab A created 'FromTabA' (storage = ['Alpha','FromTabA']); tab B then edited the body of Alpha; storage became ['Alpha']. Open the app in two tabs. Create a note in tab 1. Type in any note in tab 2 (opened before the new note existed). After 500 ms tab 2 saves its stale array, and the note created in tab 1 is gone from storage. Tab 2 shows 'Saved'. Reload and the note is lost, and nothing was reported.

index.html:19 Title and body fields have no label or name; search uses a placeholder as its only label. index.html:13, 19, 20: no <label>, aria-label or placeholder on #title and #body; #search has only a placeholder. A screen reader announces 'edit text' and 'edit text multiline' with no purpose, so the user can not tell which field is the title (WCAG 1.3.1, 3.3.2, 4.1.2).

app.js:84 Every list render destroys the focused button, so keyboard and screen-reader focus drops to the page top after selecting or deleting a note. The click handler (app.js:161-166) calls selectNote or deleteNote, both of which end in renderList, which replaces every <li> and <button> with new nodes. Nothing restores focus (focus() is called only at app.js:109 for a new note). The pagehide and blur paths are not involved. Keyboard user tabs to a note button and presses Enter. selectNote runs, the button node is removed, document.activeElement becomes <body>. The next Tab starts at the top of the page again, and the screen reader announces nothing about the opened note. The same happens after confirming Delete: focus is lost from the removed row. Opening several notes in a row needs a full re-tab from the top each time (WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order, level A).

app.js:61 A migrated or normalized notes list is never persisted at load, so storage stays in the old format until the user edits something. A user with version-0 data opens the app and only reads. Storage keeps the bare array with numeric ids, and the in-memory ids are generated fresh. A second tab or the next load can regenerate different ids for the same records.
